abstract: Most patients with disseminated nonseminomatous germ cell tumor (NSGCT) have an excellent prognosis with modern chemotherapy, although certain subgroups with a worse prognosis have been described. One such subgroup includes patients with high serum levels of the tumor marker, human chorionic gonadotropin (HCG). Sixteen patients of 104 treated for NSGCT at the CRC Wessex Medical Oncology Unit (Southampton, UK) presented with serum HCG greater than 25,000. Most of these patients exhibited features of the "choriocarcinoma syndrome" with bulky, rapidly progressive disease; frequent pulmonary, hepatic, and central nervous system complications; and a generally poorer response to standard NSGCT chemotherapy. Histologic identification of trophoblastic tumor was not made in all patients and is not essential for the diagnosis of the syndrome; indeed, closed biopsy may be contradicted in some circumstances because of the risk of hemorrhage. The NSGCT patients with poor prognosis, including patients with the choriocarcinoma syndrome, must be clearly identified in order to improve management and, eventually, cure rates.
abstract_ja: 英国Southamptonの CRC Wessex 腫瘍内科では、非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍(NSGCT)として治療した104例のうち16例が、血清hCG 25,000超を示した。これらの患者の多くは「絨毛癌症候群」の特徴を示し、腫瘍は急速に進行して増大しており、肺・肝・中枢神経系の合併症が頻繁に認められ、標準的なNSGCT化学療法への反応も概して不良であった。絨毛芽腫性腫瘍の組織学的な確認は必ずしも行われておらず、症候群の診断に不可欠ではない。実際、出血の危険から閉鎖生検が禁忌となる場合もある。予後不良のNSGCT患者(絨毛癌症候群の患者を含む)を明確に同定し、治療成績と治癒率を向上させる必要がある。
